title: Annotatio III §.III: SPECIALIOR ansa — Greek emphatic μεταβολή-terms for relative / mystic mutation, not substance
pass_a_gloss: §. III. A MORE SPECIAL handle was given to Transsubstantiation by various terms more emphatic, devised by the Fathers (especially the Greeks) according to the genius of the language, by which they were wont to designate specifically that mutation — partly relative with respect to the thing signified, partly mystic with respect to the communicating faithful — coupled to the Eucharistic bread through and after consecration; such as are recited as observed by our Author at pp. 450 & 480, and also by Salmasius in the Tractate on Transsubstantiation p. 1: namely μεταβολή, μεταμόρφωσις, μεταποίησις, μεταστοιχείωσις, μετατύπωσις, μεταρρυθμισμός, μετασκεύασις; and each is further assigned to its own Authors by John Johnston, De Communione ch. 3 p. 113. These terms, understood by the Fathers of a moral and σχετική mutation, in time generated in others the opinion of a substantial mutation.
pass_b_english: §.III SPECIALIOR handle: Greek emphatic change-terms (metabole, metamorphosis, metapoiesis, metastoicheiosis, metatyposis, metarrhythmismos, metaskeuasis) for a mutation relative to the thing signified and mystic for communicants — cited via our Author, Salmasius, Johnston.
Fathers meant moral and schetic (relative) change; later readers bred a substantial-mutation opinion from those words.
source_text: §. III. SPECIALIOR Transsubstantiationi ansa data fuit per varios Patrum, maximè Græcorum ἐμφατικωτέρας, pro genio linguæ, excogitatos terminos, quibus in specie mutationem istam, relativam partim, respectu scil. rei signatæ, partim mysticam, respectu communicantium fidelium, pani Eucharistico per & post consecrationem copulatam, designare soliti sunt, quales Autori nostro observati recitantur p. 450 & 480 necnon Salmasio in Tractat. de Transsubst. p. 1. μεταβολή scil. μεταμόρφωσις, μεταποίησις, μεταστοιχείωσις, μετατύπωσις, μεταρρυθμισμός, μετασκεύασις; singuli præterea propriis suis Autoribus tribuuntur à Joh. Jonstono de Communione c. 3. p. 113. Hi termini de morali & σχετικῇ mutatione à Patribus intellecti, substantialis mutationis opinionem aliis, procedente tempore, ingenerarunt.
